sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Passive Holding of Subsidiary Shares and Corporate Dividends

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA), in force 2014
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Applicable bilateral income tax conventions (DTAAs) depend upon the country of residence of the equity holders

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), including Alberta unlimited liability corporation (ULC) provisions and s. 120 regarding corporate records; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; Corruption of Foreign Public Officials Act, SC 1998, c 34; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp.). Alberta's beneficial-ownership transparency rules under the ABCA require the maintenance of a register of individuals with significant control (ISC), accessible to law enforcement and prescribed authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certificate of good standing / certificate of status
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada acceded effective 11 January 2024) or consular legalization for non-Hague countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of Articles of Incorporation and Certificate of Incorporation of the Alberta ULC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / consular legalization according to destination jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized register of individuals with significant control (ISC register) with ownership breakdown
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Alberta ULC compliance officer / legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, plus apostille or consular legalization if required by a foreign court or financial institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized identity, address, and PEP/sanctions verification pack for all UBOs and directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified notary public in the UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified English/French translation, or consular legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney and board authorization for pre-incorporation signing by foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary / notary public of the incorporating shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille / consular legalization by the Embassy of Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, and UBOs against the UN Consolidated List, Canadian regulations under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Criminal Code anti-terrorism listings, and Global Affairs Canada autonomous sanctions; the OFAC SDN list is also screened as prudent international banking and counterparty practice. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be identified, approved, and placed under enhanced due diligence; non-face-to-face clients require enhanced verification. Records of all screening, searches, and risk assessments must be retained for at least five years under the PCMLTFA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registries, Service Alberta (CORES e-services); NUANS name search through a Crown-authorized Alberta registry agent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate name must be capable of being expressed in the Roman alphabet; accents and common punctuation are allowed, but the name must be distinct and not confusingly similar to an existing name. Where the entity uses unlimited liability, the legal element must indicate such liability, e.g., "Unlimited Liability Corporation", "Corporation", "Limited", "Limited Liability Partnership" or the appropriate abbreviation such as "ULC", as authorized by the ABCA.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may correct and resubmit the name request through the same registry channel or file a written reconsideration request with Service Alberta within 30 days of the rejection. If Service Alberta upholds the refusal on statutory grounds, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta. It is prudent to reserve two to three alternative names at the initial filing and to file the incorporation within the 90-day reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only when a licensed registered agent provides a physical Alberta street address for service of process during normal business hours; a mere postal box or mail-forwarding virtual office does not satisfy the ABCA registered office requirement. For a passive holding SPV, a professional registered-agent address with virtual access is commonly accepted by Alberta registry and commercial banks, provided that the physical presence and agent duties are real and maintained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: estimated 5-10% probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first three years for a passive equity holding ULC; the probability may increase to 15-20% if there are trigger events such as changes in control, non-resident directors, tax structure concerns, or adverse AML/CFT screening findings.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS name search and name reservation
Registration of Alberta ULC Articles of Incorporation under ABCA
Registered office and registered agent for first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate service provider / registered agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation of ULC articles, by-laws, shareholder resolutions, and ISC register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate, fixed fee for equity holding SPV

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT and sanctions/PEP screening of UBOs, directors, and parent entities
Notarization, apostille, and consular legalization of corporate and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, foreign ministry (apostille issuer), or Canadian consulate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate minute book, share certificates, and electronic record system
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm or corporate records vendor

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation income tax review of ULC pass-through status and Canadian withholding exposures

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 6, 9, 15.1-15.6 (Unlimited Liability Corporation provisions), 101 (registered office), 213-214 (annual return)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form N1) filed under s. 9 of the ABCA, incorporating the ULC election and the designation 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company'
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up share capital is prescribed; the ULC may commence with a single share without par value; no escrow account or capital deposit is required at incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, THAT the incorporation of the Corporation as an unlimited liability corporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) is ratified and the Articles of Incorporation and Certificate of Incorporation are approved.

RESOLVED, THAT the by-laws presented are adopted and the registered office is established at the address in the Articles.

RESOLVED, THAT the share subscriptions are approved and certificates be issued per the share register.

RESOLVED, THAT [Name] is appointed President and [Name] Secretary-Treasurer, with authority to open bank accounts and complete registrations.

RESOLVED, THAT all incorporator actions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta - NUANS search through authorized Registry service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Procure a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report for the proposed name. Ensure the name contains a distinctive element and a mandatory corporate designation permitted for a ULC ('ULC', 'Unlimited Liability Company', or approved equivalent). The name reservation is valid for 90 days and must be attached to the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search request (Form NUS-1 or service-provider portal)
Contact details of the requesting incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, a written reconsideration request may be filed with the Registry within the stated response period, or a revised name may be submitted for a new NUANS search before the 90-day window lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of ULC Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator (subscriber) and eventual filing party at Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation on the prescribed Form N1. Include the ULC election required by s. 15.1 ABCA, the authorized share structure (class and maximum number of shares), any restrictions on share classes (including 'inside' and 'outside' classes used for Canadian GST/ITC tracking where applicable), and the physical Alberta registered office address. The incorporator executes the articles with the statutory declaration of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Physical registered office address in Alberta (no post-office box)
Consent of directors named in the articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a notice of deficiency, the incorporator may file corrective amended articles or submit written representations within the statutory response period; Registry service providers can assist with same-day refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic or Paper Lodgement and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (paper lodgement at the Registry office or electronic filing through an authorized corporate Registry service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation with the prescribed incorporation fee (approximately CA$400 plus CA$50 name search). The Registrar reviews the articles against ABCA requirements and, upon approval, issues the Certificate of Incorporation, the legal 'birth' of the ULC. Request certified copies for the minute book and bank account opening.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (Form N1) signed by the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is withheld pending clarification, respond to the Registry's query with corrected information or documentation in writing within the stated period; if the certificate is refused, recompose the articles and re-file with a fresh fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inaugural Board Resolution and Adoption of By-Law No. 1
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the ULC (first directors named in the articles or appointed by the incorporator)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or execute the written First Board Resolution. Adopt By-law No. 1, fix the registered office, approve the form of share certificates, appoint officers, designate banking signatories, and give direction to open the corporate bank account and complete tax registrations. Minutes must be signed and retained in the minute book.
required_dossiers: Written resolution or minutes of the organizational meeting
Consent to act as registered office provider (if different from the corporate office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If unanimous board approval is unattainable, the board may reconvene with the requisite quorum or the incorporator may remove and replace non-participating first directors under s. 13 ABCA and execute a fresh resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Subscription, Issuance and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Corporate Secretary of the ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approve the share subscriptions from the founders or parent entity, issue the share certificates, and open the register of members. Populate the registers of directors, registered office, and material contracts in the minute book. For ULCs, annotate the shareholder exposure language confirming that shareholders are liable for the corporation's debts to the extent provided under s. 15.1 ABCA.
required_dossiers: Register of members and register of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Incorrect share certificates may be cancelled and reissued by board resolution; if the share structure must be amended, filed Articles of Amendment with the Registry cure the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online) and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register on CRA's Business Registration Online to obtain the federal Business Number and the Corporate Income Tax program account (RD). Register for the Alberta Corporate Tax account through the same joint national registration process. GST/HST registration is not mandatory for a passive holding SPV unless the subsidiary group is a registrant and the SPV's shareholding attracts required registration; evaluate at filing. Record the BN on all bank and Registry filings.
required_dossiers: Directors' legal names, home addresses, and personal identification (SIN/ITN)
Ownership and governance organogram of the parent entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA requests additional information, answer within the 30-day notice window via the Business Window (1-800-959-5525) or through an accountant with signed authorization; delays in receiving the BN-issued letters do not suspend the corporation's obligation to file returns once accounts are active.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Compliance, Annual Return and AML-Ready Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; FINTRAC-oriented recordkeeping reviewed by the board
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first Alberta Annual Return (Form AN1) within 30 days of the first anniversary of incorporation and annually thereafter; maintain the registered office records and minute book at the Alberta office; prepare a FINTRAC-style customer due diligence file on beneficial shareholders to support the Medium-Risk Enhanced banking profile at the target bank; obtain municipal business licence and WCB-Alberta confirmations only if the SPV later hires employees or leases physical space.
required_dossiers: Alberta Annual Return (Form AN1) and filing fee
CDD/KYC file (passport, proof of address, source of funds for ultimate shareholders)
Corporate record book prepared for bank due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late annual return penalties may be waived under the Registrar's late-filing relief, or the corporation may be reinstated after administrative dissolution by filing arrears, the reinstatement application, and restoration fees.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for passive equity holding (ISIC 6420 / NAICS 551112); municipal 'General Business Licence' may be obtained at the City of Calgary or City of Edmonton business licensing centre only if a physical office is opened.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industry operating or manufacturing permit is required for a pure equity-holding SPV; the Certificate of Incorporation and corporate registration constitute the sole formation approvals.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no physical works, emissions or environmental effects; passive holding of subsidiary shares does not constitute a mandatory or exempt activity under the Environmental Assessment (Mandatory and Exempt Activities) Regulation (AR 83/2011)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge thresholds apply. If an administrative office is leased, comply with municipal wastewater/stormwater bylaws, provincial waste segregation and disposal rules under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, and indoor-air/VOC limits only where landlord-controlled HVAC systems are governed by municipal maintenance standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required at formation for a passive holding SPV. If employees are engaged or premises are leased, obtain: (i) landlord's certificate of occupancy and fire-code compliance; (ii) Alberta Fire Safety inspection clearance for the leased office; and (iii) WCB-Alberta account registration or exemption filing under the Workers' Compensation Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — federal income tax and GST/HST; CRA collects Alberta corporate income tax on behalf of the Province under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act via the tax collection agreement. Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA) administers provincial non-income taxes. CRA digital portals: Business Registration Online (BRO), My Business Account (MyBA), GST/HST NETFILE.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: incorporate the ULC under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) at the Alberta Corporate Registry (registered agent filing). Step 2: obtain the 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1; a non-resident parent is disclosed, but the ULC is a Canadian-resident corporation. Step 3: activate program accounts on the BN — RP (corporate income tax, automatic), RT (GST/HST, only if registrant), RC (payroll, if employees). Step 4: file annual T2 Corporation Income Tax Return within 6 months of fiscal year-end and remit any Alberta/federal tax within 2 months of year-end. Step 5: file Form T1134 (information return re foreign affiliates) and T106 (cross-border reportable transactions) if applicable. A foreign entity with no Canadian presence deriving only Canadian dividends needs a BN only for Part XIII withholding compliance, using the same RC1/Non-Resident Registration route.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — under the Income Tax Act (Canada), an Alberta ULC is a corporation resident in Canada, taxed on worldwide income (federal general rate 15% plus Alberta general rate 8%, combined 23%). The ULC is not fiscally transparent in Canada. Pass_Through_Eligible status applies only for U.S. federal tax purposes (IRS Form 8832 check-the-box), creating a hybrid entity; this does not alter Canadian entity-level taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regime. Key ULC-relevant mechanics: (i) U.S. shareholders may file IRS Form 8832 to treat the ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership for U.S. tax purposes, subject to Canada-U.S. Tax Treaty Article IV(6)(b) fiscally-transparent provisions; (ii) intercorporate dividend deduction under ITA s. 112(1) (statutory, no election) because the ULC is a Canadian corporation; (iii) foreign affiliate surplus election/mechanics under ITA s. 113(1) with Form T1134 reporting; (iv) ITA s. 216 election for non-resident rental income and s. 217 employment income (not applicable to pure holding SPV); (v) anti-hybrid mismatch restrictions in ITA ss. 18.4, 18.5, 95 and s. 162(12), which may deny deductions for interest/royalty flows to hybrid arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST — no provincial sales tax or HST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — cumulative worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated supplies) made in any single calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters triggers mandatory GST/HST registration (Excise Tax Act s. 240). Dividend income and share-sale gains are exempt financial services, so a pure equity holding SPV without fee income is generally not a registrant.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control/API mandate exists in Canada or Alberta. CRA requires mandatory electronic filing (GST/HST NETFILE) for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1,000,000, and mandatory T2 e-filing for corporations with gross revenue over CAD 1,000,000. Peppol-based Pan-Canadian e-invoicing is voluntary (CRA 2024–2025 pilot), with no statutory clearance obligation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI Part V s. 7 when the supplier (or an agent) exports goods to a destination outside Canada, with continuous-journey evidence and proof of export. Services: zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident person not present in Canada, unless the non-resident is a GST/HST registrant, the service is performed for an individual in Canada, or the service relates to Canadian real property. A pure equity holding SPV's dividend income is an exempt financial service (Schedule V Part VII), not zero-rated, so GST/HST does not apply to dividend flows.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Canada B13A/CAED; ACE/AES where goods transit the United States)
Bill of Lading / air waybill / CMR carrier evidence of export
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103/bank statement evidencing export proceeds repatriation into Canada
Underlying contracts, purchase orders, insurance certificates, and CRA books-and-records retention under ETA s. 286 (six years)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA reassessment windows: 3 years for income tax (ITA s. 152(4)) and 4 years for GST/HST (ETA s. 298), extended up to 10 years or indefinitely for misrepresentation or fraud. Penalties: ITA s. 163(2) gross-negligence misrepresentation — 25% of understated tax; ETA s. 280 failure to file/remit — 1% of net tax plus 25% per month (maximum 12 months, minimum CAD 100); ETA s. 285 false statements — greater of CAD 100 and 25% of tax; ETA s. 327 criminal evasion — fines up to 250% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; ITA ss. 238/239 criminal evasion — 50%–200% fines and imprisonment up to 5 years. Improper export zero-rating is reversed on audit: the supply becomes taxable, ITCs are denied, interest (ETA s. 296) and penalties apply. The 180-day repatriation benchmark is an evidentiary best practice for proving payment/receipt in export substantiation, not a statutory deadline under the ETA or ITA.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); with the Department of Finance Canada as the federal FX policy authority, OSFI as prudential bank regulator, and FINTRAC as AML/ATF supervisor.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is a floating, fully convertible currency. Canada maintains no exchange-control restrictions applicable to current-account or capital-account transactions, and no separate approval is required for dividend remittances, equity injections, or intercompany debt servicing by an Alberta ULC. Any withholding tax exposure arises under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (sections 212 and 215), not under FX regulations. A pure equity-holding SPV may freely repatriate profits, repay shareholder loans, and purchase foreign currency from a Schedule I/II Canadian bank at commercial rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose statutory surrender timelines or mandatory conversion ratios on export receipts. A Canadian exporter/SPV may hold foreign currency in Canadian or offshore accounts. Reporting obligations are limited to FINTRAC large cash/electronic funds transfer reports (CAD 10,000), CRA foreign income/asset reporting (Form T1135 where applicable), and, for goods exports, Export and Import Permits Act compliance where controlled goods are involved.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium as a primary treasury rail. A non-Canadian electronic money institution (EMI) is not authorized under the Bank Act to take deposits or operate as a bank in Canada. Such an entity may only provide ancillary payment services if registered as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC and compliant with provincial consumer-protection laws; it cannot substitute for a Canadian bank account for capital escrow, ULC statutory filings, or high-value clearing. For cross-border disbursements, a FINTRAC-registered MSB can be used as a secondary payout rail, but primary liquidity must remain in a Canadian prudence-regulated bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Not statutorily mandated, but practically required. OSFI/FINTRAC do not require physical attendance when enhanced due diligence is satisfied through verified video/KYC, but most Canadian Schedule I banks will demand a physical in-branch interview for non-resident-owned, unlimited-liability entities, at least for the ultimate beneficial owner and a signing director. Remote opening is sometimes available to pre-approved jurisdictions with independent electronic identity verification; an Alberta ULC will typically receive enhanced risk treatment and may require a local director or commercial account manager to complete the interview in Calgary or Edmonton.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited liability nature of the ULC creating uncertainty on personal exposure and control rights.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certified Articles of Incorporation/Amalgamation, the ULC declaration/notice, unanimous shareholder agreement, authorized share capital schedule, register of directors, and a board resolution confirming that treasury transactions are limited to passive equity holding and are not to create creditor recourse beyond ordinary-course trade payables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity where shares are held through a non-resident parent or trust.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver an ownership chart with each intervening entity's corporate number and registered office, government-issued photo ID and residential address for all direct/indirect 25%+ holders and controlling persons, completed beneficial ownership attestation, and FINTRAC-required individual identity records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth concerns for a high-value inbound equity contribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a source-of-funds letter from the remitting parent/shareholder, audited or internally prepared parent financial statements, bank statements showing a clear origination trail, executed share subscription agreement, currency conversion confirmation, and payment routing details (SWIFT MT103) tracing funds to the ULC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax transparency and potential treaty-shopping or withholding structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide Canadian tax registration number (if any), CRA determination letters, tax residency certificate of the shareholder, income tax treaty analysis showing economic substance, board minutes approving commercial rationale, and Part XIII withholding self-assessment or applicable treaty rate analysis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Enhanced risk due to high-risk jurisdiction, PEP involvement, or cryptocurrency-linked fund flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a transaction-specific compliance memorandum, admissible source-of-wealth reports from independent counsel/accountants, negative news and sanctions screening results, senior management approval under the bank's high-risk customer framework, and ongoing transaction monitoring commitments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the inbound equity capital injection via SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident parent's bank to the ULC's Canadian-dollar account at a Canadian Schedule I bank. Field 50K must identify the originating shareholder/remitter; field 59 must show the ULC's legal name and account number; field 70 should state 'ULC share subscription - equity contribution - [Alberta corporate access number]' to avoid misclassification as revenue. Canadian banks do not apply a single statutory purpose code, but internal corporate banking codes such as 'TRF/INV' are commonly used for inward investment. Canadian banks require a board resolution, share subscription agreement and source-of-funds evidence before accepting the inward credit if the amount exceeds FINTRAC's reportable threshold; where the parent is in a restricted/high-risk jurisdiction, pre-approval and the completion of enhanced due diligence should occur before the wire is sent. No Bank of Canada approval is needed, but Investment Canada Act notification thresholds should be reviewed where the inbound contribution is used to acquire control of an existing Canadian business.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements from the ULC (dividends, shareholder loan repayments, service payments or acquisition consideration) should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for direct correspondent-beneficiary transfers and MT202 COV for cover payments; Canadian-dollar domestic legs may settle through Payments Canada's Lynx RTGS. For trade-related disbursements, a commercial letter of credit (MT700/MT707) issued under UCP600, confirmation by a foreign bank, and customary presentation through the bank's trade services desk are the recognized clearing rails. All outbound payments must include correct tax withholding under Part XIII and CRA NR4 reporting if payable to non-residents, plus FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting for CAD 10,000+ transactions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD (and other liquid currencies) foreign exchange forward contract
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for restricted or non-deliverable counterparty currencies
Cross-currency swap / cross-currency basis swap to hedge long-term equity and intercompany loan exposure
Vanilla foreign-exchange options and zero-cost/structured collar arrangements
FX swap / rollover swap used to manage funding-date mismatches on trade settlements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Business Corporations Act (Alberta), s.266) — Corporate Registry Declaration of Status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following each anniversary of incorporation (e.g., 15 Jan incorporation → 16 Mar due date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing blocks certificates of compliance/good standing; prolonged default (typically 1–2 consecutive years) triggers a Notice of Intended Dissolution and administrative strike-off; reinstatement requires arrears plus statutory reinstatement fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Income Tax Act, s.150(1)) incl. Schedule 5 Alberta Allocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Corporate Tax Services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the ULC's taxation year-end (a strict 31 Dec year-end yields a 30 Jun due date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month (max 12 months); a minimum CAD 100 penalty applies to nil-balance returns; chronic default can trigger a CRA formal demand, jeopardy assessment, and extension of the normal reassessment period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T1134 Information Return for Foreign Affiliates (Income Tax Act, ss.233.4–233.5)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — International and Non-Resident Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the T2 due date (6 months after the ULC's taxation year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of CAD 100 per day late (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 per reporting year); deliberate omission or gross negligence attracts higher fines and indefinitely extends CRA's reassessment window.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory asset/revenue threshold under the ABCA. Each corporation must appoint a licensed auditor at the annual meeting, but a private, non-distributing Alberta ULC may waive the audit via unanimous shareholder consent—the standard step for a single-parent pure equity HoldCo. Absent this waiver, an independent CPA audit is mandatory each fiscal year and the audited statements must be sent to shareholders at least 21 days before the AGM.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) for publicly accountable enterprises and IFRS-based consolidated groups; ASPE (Part II) is the default Canadian private-enterprise GAAP; a US-parented ULC may maintain US GAAP internal books while reconciling to Canadian tax basis for CRA reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The ULC must maintain an ongoing Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC), recording any qualifying natural person (≥25% shares, votes, or de facto control) and updating the register within 15 days of any share-transfer or acquisition. The ISC register is kept at the Alberta registered office, subject to inspection, and the annual-return confirmation process requires corporate records (including ISC data) to stay current. Non-compliance is an offence with fines up to CAD 200,000 and/or up to 6 months' imprisonment.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200–900 per year (CAD 270–1,250) for an Alberta registered office address plus registered agent/secretarial services; mid-market engagements typically run USD 300–600.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 where the unanimous consent audit waiver is in place (standard for a single-parent pure equity ULC); USD 8,000–20,000 (CAD 11,000–27,000) for a stand-alone certified audit if the waiver is not adopted.
